INDIANAPOLIS 46204
ROOM 212, STATE HOUSE 633-5610
June 21, 1972
STATE BUDGET AGENCY
Indiana State Clearinghouse
Review # 7203470000
Department of Natural Resources - Division of Nature Preserves
I concur with the two objectives shown under 3 Summary, with the following comment.
More definite criteria needs to be formulated on how it will be determined when a species or subspecies is becoming endangered. What population level by species is critical?
Many endangered species, especially birds, are migratory and would fall under the blanket protection now given such species by the Federal Government. In many cases in the past, State protection actually protected more species than Federal regualtions until their recent revision.
However, there are some present and future endangered species that are more sedentary and may exist in a limited habitat within one State. This proposed legislation will probably be objected to by States as an abrogation of the states traditional ownership of resident wildlife on all lands regardless of public or private ownership.
Where such ranges are restricted, this Act should include concurring state legislation.
In such cases, the bill should also include consultation of the Federal Agency with the appropriate State Agency.
Department of Natural Resources - Fish and Game Division
We are critical of the implied ability of the Federal Government to manage species that could become endangered but are not at the present time.
We do not favor removing listed endangered species from the States' jurisdiction, but feel Federal assistance maybe warrented in some circumstances.
